finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test passes a user-supplied callback URL straight to axios.post, enabling full SSRF (internal services, cloud metadata, etc.). The response status is returned to the caller, so it also works as a port/host oracle.
finding.source: req.body.callback (POST body on the public router `pub`)

trace.note: pub router is created with no auth middleware
URL is passed unvalidated to axios.post
upstream status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no DNS-rebind protection, and no redirect restriction (axios follows redirects by default). requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router (routes.js:12), not to pub. I could not see how the routers are mounted, because this is the only file in the directory.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post and returns the status. The `pub` router (routes.js:4) has no auth middleware, since requireAdmin is applied only to `admin` at routes.js:12. The mounting of the routers is not visible, so an auth layer applied at mount time can't be ruled out, but nothing in the available code guards this route.

finding.claim: GET /diagnostics/fetch passes a user-supplied URL straight to axios.get, so an admin can make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs. It is gated by requireAdmin, so it is lower severity, but still an SSRF if an admin account is compromised or an admin is tricked via CSRF.
finding.source: req.query.url (query string on the admin router)

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) restricts the route to session role 'admin'
URL is passed unvalidated to axios.get
upstream status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) checks req.session.role === 'admin'. There is no URL scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP blocking, and no redirect restriction. The route is a GET, so a CSRF-style trigger is possible depending on session cookie settings. Only the status code is returned, so it is a blind-ish SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) restricts the route to session role 'admin'. It is an authorization gate, not a URL validator, so no URL, host or scheme validation exists.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:12-16), but req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after requireAdmin (routes.js:8, 12), so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control it. The CSRF path is speculative, because no session cookie settings or CSRF protection appear in this code.
